advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether AGENTS.md:191 should also mention the Codex `codex mcp list` diagnostic now that Serena is registered for Codex.
evidence: AGENTS.md:191: "Evidence and reproductions: `docs/code-navigation.md`; if Serena is absent, `claude mcp get serena`."

Ticket comment notes the AGENTS.md update was deferred: "Review advisory to update AGENTS.md was deferred to preserve the ticket's signed single-file scope" — the Codex diagnostic is `codex mcp list`, per the ticket's own recovery command.
advisory.finding: AGENTS.md's Serena recovery guidance names only the Claude-specific diagnostic `claude mcp get serena` and is not updated to reference the Codex equivalent now that Serena is registered for Codex via .codex/config.toml.
scenarios: A Codex (non-Claude) contributor whose Serena server fails to start reads AGENTS.md and only finds a Claude-only diagnostic command, which does not apply to their agent.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin serena's transitive dependencies (e.g. via a lockfile / uv --locked) rather than resolving them at runtime.
evidence: uvx resolves and installs serena plus its transitive deps at run time with no accompanying lockfile committed in this change
No accompanying note or record of the dependency's license or provenance review in the diff
advisory.finding: The Serena MCP dependency is fetched via `uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@<sha>` with no lockfile or hash pinning for transitive dependencies, so the resolved Python dependency tree is unpinned and non-reproducible.
merged_from: The new MCP server pulls executable code from a third-party GitHub org (oraios/serena) with no provenance/integrity verification beyond the git ref, and no license posture is documented for the introduced dependency.
scenarios: A transitive dependency of serena is compromised or yanked, altering behavior of the MCP server that runs with tool access
